answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by paying every identity from one fixed pool split by verified work: each newcomer posts graded original work plus a bond under basalt-hard rules, then takes a share in proportion to that work. A whisper of profit lures a farm in, but each extra head dilutes every slice, so the thousandth fake earns less than its own verification cost — the attacker's own demand bends the curve against it, and bulk farming turns umber-dark unprofitable.
